status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: OpenAI and Discourse remediated the reported issues after disclosure. This is a concrete repair of the access pathway affecting AI service accounts; it does not establish that every possible connected-service exposure was examined.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: Authorised researchers demonstrated that the exploit chain exposed authentication material and enabled access to affected ChatGPT or Codex accounts. The affected AI services did not preserve their account security boundary. This is distinct from misconduct by the assisting Claude models.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence exposes two governance surfaces. First, cyber-capable models made available for qualified security work can materially increase exploit-development capability, so access must be tied to authorisation, target scope, containment, monitoring and disclosure conditions. Second, the exploit chain raises identity, session and delegated-authority questions because compromise of one authentication surface reportedly propagated into more consequential OpenAI products and potentially connected services. Successful authorised security research is not itself model misbehaviour, and Claude's assistance does not establish that it violated an internal governance boundary. Human-led authorized research, demonstrated access and later remediation remain separate resolved-no-mapping components. Claude assistance does not establish autonomous target selection or an AI-governance failure; every testing scope and connected-service exposure is not independently determined.
conclusion_change.new: Authorised AI-assisted research demonstrated an account-security weakness affecting AI services. The affected providers repaired the reported issues. The finding concerns victim-service security, while Claude’s assistance remains authorised research rather than established model misconduct. The full testing scope and every connected-service exposure remain bounded by the sources.
